title: Adaptation Versus Mitigation Climate Finance and Ecological Footprint in Sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence from Method of Moments Quantile Regression
content: Climate finance to Sub-Saharan Africa has grown, yet the region's ecological footprint continues to exceed its biocapacity. Most studies treat climate finance as a single aggregate and estimate average effects. This study asks whether adaptation and mitigation finance affect ecological pressure differently and whether their effects vary between low-footprint and high-footprint countries. Using a panel of 48 Sub-Saharan African countries over 2010 to 2022, it measures adaptation and mitigation finance as disbursements per capita from the OECD Climate-Related Development Finance database and ecological footprint per capita from the National Footprint and Biocapacity Accounts. After tests for cross-sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, unit roots and cointegration, the study applies the Method of Moments Quantile Regression, tests the equality of the two finance coefficients at each quantile, and separates the carbon and land-based footprint components. Mitigation finance reduces the ecological footprint, with effects that grow toward the upper quantiles, whereas adaptation finance reduces it mainly at the lower and middle quantiles. The two effects differ significantly at the tails of the distribution. The findings support allocating each stream according to a country's position in the footprint distribution.
